questions.stem:
A test statistic has a distribution $\mathrm{B}(25, p)$.

Given that

$\mathrm{H_0}: p=0.5 \quad \mathrm{H_1}: p \neq 0.5$

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) find the critical region for the test statistic such that the probability in each tail is as close as possible to 2.5%. (3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $X\sim \mathrm{B}(25,0.5)$ M1 (may be implied by calculations in part a or b)
$\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 7)=0.0216$
$\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 18)=0.0216$
CR $X\leqslant 7;\ \cup\ X\geqslant 18$ A1,A1
Notes: M1 - Using B(25,0.5) – may be implied by a correct critical region or by calculations in part a or b. Note just seeing either $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 7)$ or $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 18)$ scores M1 A0 A0. You may need to check their probabilities in the tables for values other than 7 or 18. 1st A1 – also allow $X<8$ or $[0,7]$ or $0\leqslant X\leqslant 7$ or $0\leqslant X<8$ oe e.g. $[0,8)$ or a full list. DO NOT allow CRs given as $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 7)$ or $7-0$ for the A mark. 2nd A1 – also allow $X>17$ or $[18,25]$ or $18\leqslant X\leqslant 25$ or $17<X\leqslant 25$ oe e.g. $(17,25]$ or a full list. DO NOT allow CRs given as $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 18)$ or $18-25$ for the A mark. SC $7\geqslant X\geqslant 18$ gains M1 A1 A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) State the probability of incorrectly rejecting $\mathrm{H_0}$ using this critical region. (2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P}(\text{rejecting } \mathrm{H_0})=0.0216+0.0216$ M1
$=0.0432$ awrt 0.0432/0.0433 A1
Notes: M1 – adding their two critical regions' probabilities together or may be awarded for awrt 0.0432. If they add their critical regions' probabilities and then go on and get a different probability as their answer then it is M0A0 e.g. $0.0216+0.0216=0.0432$ then $0.05-0.0432=0.0068$ gets M0 A0; e.g. $0.0216+0.0216=0.0432 < 0.05$ reject $\mathrm{H_0}$ gets M1 A1; e.g. $0.0216+0.0216=0.0432$ so probability of rejecting $\mathrm{H_0}$ is $1-0.0432=0.9568$ gets M0 A0.

questions.stem:
In a large restaurant an average of 3 out of every 5 customers ask for water with their meal.

A random sample of 10 customers is selected.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that

(i) exactly 6 ask for water with their meal,

(ii) less than 9 ask for water with their meal. (5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Let $X$ be the random variable the number of customers asking for water.
(i) $X\sim \mathrm{B}(10,0.6)$ B1 [or $Y\sim \mathrm{B}(10,0.4)$]
$\mathrm{P}(X=6)=(0.6)^6(0.4)^4\frac{10!}{6!4!}$ M1 [or $\mathrm{P}(Y=4)=(0.4)^4(0.6)^6\frac{10!}{6!4!}$]
$=0.2508...$ awrt 0.251 A1
(ii) $\mathrm{P}(X<9)=1-(\mathrm{P}(X=10)+\mathrm{P}(X=9))$ M1 [or $\mathrm{P}(X<9)=1-\mathrm{P}(Y\leqslant 1)$]
$=1-(0.6)^{10}-(0.6)^9(0.4)^1\frac{10!}{9!1!}$ [or $=1-0.0464$]
$=0.9536...$ awrt 0.954 A1
Notes: B1 writing or using $\mathrm{B}(10,0.6)$ / $\mathrm{B}(10,0.4)$ in either part(i) or (ii). (i) M1 $(0.6)^6(1-0.6)^4\frac{10!}{6!4!}$ Allow $^{10}C_6$ oe or writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 6)-\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 5)$ if using $\mathrm{B}(10,0.6)$ or $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 4)-\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 3)$ if using $\mathrm{B}(10,0.4)$. NB use of Poisson will gain M0A0. (ii) M1 writing or using $1-(\mathrm{P}(X=10)+\mathrm{P}(X=9))$ if using $\mathrm{B}(10,0.6)$ or $1-\mathrm{P}(Y\leqslant 1)$ if using $\mathrm{B}(10,0.4)$. NB use of Poisson will gain M0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A second random sample of 50 customers is selected.

(b) Find the smallest value of $n$ such that

$\mathrm{P}(X<n)\geqslant 0.9$

where the random variable $X$ represents the number of these customers who ask for water. (3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $X\sim \mathrm{B}(50,0.6)$
$Y\sim \mathrm{B}(50,0.4)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(X<n)\geqslant 0.9$
$\mathrm{P}(Y>50-n)\geqslant 0.9$ or $\mathrm{P}(X<34)=0.8439$ awrt 0.844 M1
$\mathrm{P}(Y\leqslant 50-n)\leqslant 0.1$ $\mathrm{P}(X<35)=0.9045$ awrt 0.904/0.905
$50-n\leqslant 15$
$n\geqslant 35$
$n=35$ A1
Notes: 1st M1 for writing or using either $\mathrm{B}(50,0.6)$ or $\mathrm{B}(50,0.4)$. 2nd M1 $\mathrm{P}(Y>50-n)\geqslant 0.9$ or $\mathrm{P}(Y\leqslant 50-n)\leqslant 0.1$ or $\mathrm{P}(X<34)=$ awrt 0.844 or $\mathrm{P}(X<35)=$ awrt 0.904/0.905 or $50-n=15$ or $50-n=16$ or $50-n\leqslant 15$ or $50-n\leqslant 16$ – allow different letters. A1 cao 35. Do not accept $n\geqslant 35$ for final A1.
SC use of normal. M1 M0 A0 for use of $\mathrm{N}(30,12)$ leading to an answer of 35.
